div.head: IV Atr 4
div.ab: Et diximus: homo qui hamsocnam faciet intra portum sine licentia et summam infracturam aget de placito ungebendeo uel qui aliquem innocentem affliget in uia regia, si iaceat, iaceat in ungildan ækere.

Et diximus: homo qui hamsocnam faciet intra portum sine licentia et summam infracturam aget de placito ungebendeo, vel qui aliquem innocentem affliget in via regia, si iaceat, iaceat in ungildan ækere.

Und wir haben bestimmt: wer innerhalb der Stadt Angriff auf jemandes Heim ohne Erlaubniss ausführt oder schwerste Verletzung [königlichen Stadtfriedens] verübt an einem [von ihm noch] nicht zum Rechtsgang aufgeforderten[?], oder wer einen Unschuldigen auf der königlichen [Heer]strasse angreift, wenn er dabei getödtet wird, liege er in dem nicht [durch Wergeld] entgoltenen [unehrlichen] Felde.

And we have determined: whoever attacks someone's home within the town without permission, or commits the gravest breach [of the king's town-peace] against someone not [yet] summoned [by him] to legal process[?], or whoever attacks an innocent person on the king's highway, if he is killed in doing so, let him lie in the field that is not paid for [by wergild, i.e. dishonoured].

And we have decreed that a man who, within the town, makes forcible entry into another man’s house without permission and commits a breach of the peace of the worst kind… and he who assaults an innocent person on the king’s highway, if he is slain, shall lie in an unhonoured grave.
div.note: ‘ungebendeo’ should perhaps be corrected to ‘rihtes ungebedene’ (Liebermann).

Das Original hatte -bryce; für heah- setzt zwar Q öfter summus; allein *heahbryce (vgl. heahsynn ‘schwere Sünde’) ist nicht nachgewiesen. Für fullbryce, -brecan (s. d. Wb) setzt Q zwar eher plena, doch passt wohl nur dieser Sinn im Ggs. zur Halbverletzung (s. d. Gl) ohne Totschlag. Was aber verletzt war, sagt der Q-Text nicht; es muss im Original ausgedrückt gewesen sein: vielleicht mund, borg, grið, d. i. Frieden mit dem Sondersinne ‘Königschutz’; man streiche in meiner [Klammer]: ‘Stadt’

The original had -bryce; it is true that Q often puts summus for heah-; but *heahbryce (cf. heahsynn ‘grave sin’) is not attested. For fullbryce, -brecan (see that word in Wb) Q would, it is true, rather put plena, yet probably only this sense fits, in contrast to half-breach (see that word in Gl) without homicide. What was violated, however, the Q text does not say; it must have been expressed in the original: perhaps mund, borg, grið, i.e. peace in the special sense of ‘king's protection’; in my [bracket] delete ‘Stadt’
Vielleicht steht de für den Gen. des Erbetenen (oder für Präp. ymb oder for davor) im Agsächs. Oder aber de übersetzt eine Agsächs. Präposition, die besagte, gegen wen der Friedbruch zielte

Perhaps de stands for the genitive of the thing requested (or for a preposition ymb or for before it) in the Anglo-Saxon. Or else de translates an Anglo-Saxon preposition stating against whom the breach of the peace was directed

Wie rihtes biddan oft vorkommt, so ist gemoles (spræce) biddan ‘zum Gericht (Prozess) auffordern’ denkbar; jenes hätte Q de placito übersetzt; unbeden, unabeden ist belegt, ungebeden also nicht auffallend.—Lappenberg vermutet ungewened ‘unerwartet’, Thorpe und Toller ungeboden ‘unvorgeladen, ungeboten Ding’ (vgl. Gl Gericht 9k); Steenstrup (Danelag 358) versteht dies als sine licentia, Dänisch af þingi ubedhen

Just as rihtes biddan occurs frequently, so gemoles (spræce) biddan ‘to call for a court (a suit)’ is conceivable; Q would have translated that as de placito; unbeden, unabeden is attested, so ungebeden is not surprising.—Lappenberg conjectures ungewened ‘unexpected’, Thorpe and Toller ungeboden ‘unsummoned, an unsummoned court’ (cf. Gl Gericht 9k); Steenstrup (Danelag 358) understands this as sine licentia, Danish af þingi ubedhen
Vgl. Gl Strasse 7. 8. Vielleicht las Original cyncstræt oder ähnlich ebd. o. II S. 674 Z. 2ff.; s. jedoch Gl Rechtssperrung 4
Cf. Gl Strasse 7. 8. Perhaps the original read cyncstræt or similar, ibid. above II p. 674 ll. 2ff.; see, however, Gl Rechtssperrung 4
Original hatte licge; s. d. Wb 7
The original had licge; see that word in Wb 7
orgilde will ohne Not ändern Schmid; Steenstrup Danelag 356 weist ‘i ugildum akri’ im Altnordischen Recht nach; vgl. Grab 2b
Schmid needlessly wishes to alter orgilde; Steenstrup Danelag 356 points to ‘i ugildum akri’ in Old Norse law; cf. Grab 2b
i.e. apparently the king and his councillors.
summam infracturam, i.e. A.S. -bryce. Q does not say what was violated, but the original probably had mund, borg or grið. Breach of the peace with homicide is probably intended.

The word ungebendeo or ungebendro is obscure and in all probability corrupt. Thorpe (Glossary, s.v.) and BT. p. 1106 suggest ungeboden, i.e. unsummoned, unbidden, while Steenstrup (Danelag, p. 358) takes the phrase as equivalent to sine licentia placiti and compares it with the Danish af þingi unbedhen. Liebermann suggests that the original A.S. text may have read gemotes (spræce) ungebeden (cf. placitum translating A.S. gemot, Af. 38 Q; II As. 20 Q; translating spræc, I Edw. Pre. Q; also the use of the phrase rihtes gebeden, II Cn. 19). His translation is: ‘[wer] schwerste Verletzung verübt an einem [von ihm noch] nicht zum Rechtsgang aufgeforderten (?).’

Cf. Hn. 80, 2 where forestal is explained as in via regis assultus. Liebermann points out that forsteall, hamsocn and griðbryce are three of the crimes for which £5 must be paid according to Hn 12, 2; 35, 2; DB. i. 172 a, 1; 252 a, 1.

A Scandinavian expression (i úgildum akri), see Steenstrup, Danelag, p. 356. The word úgildr strictly means that for which no wergeld is paid, and the phrase may therefore mean that he shall lie in the ground used for those for whom no wergeld is paid. On the other hand it is possible that the precise significance originally attaching to the word may have been lost.
